mechanism_narrative: Persistent low TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suppresses discretionary trips and in-person shopping, so RETAIL_REC remains below its recent 4-week average over the next month. The mechanism is a lagged spillover from reduced commuting into fewer retail visits.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed near -55 to -58 and WORKPLACES remained negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain at or below their current depressed levels for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above its baseline and stays elevated, household time at home substitutes away from shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks. This effect is strongest when WORKPLACES do not rebound at the same time.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +8 while WORKPLACES remains below -20
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was positive in all four weeks while WORKPLACES stayed negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +8 and WORKPLACES staying below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after a weak patch signals more essential errand trips and nearby mixed-purpose travel, which spills over into retail visits over the following week. The effect is short-horizon and should be visible first in footfall-sensitive retail areas.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns from negative to rising week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from 3.6 to -6.0 across the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM stops falling and starts rising week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If transit mobility begins recovering from its current trough, the public is resuming cross-town movement that supports shopping trips and dining-linked retail. A weekly rise in TRANSIT should translate into a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points from the prior week after remaining below -50
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -50.4 and -58.3 in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean even after TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points from a sub -50 baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A strong PARKS rebound diverts leisure time toward outdoor recreation and away from retail complexes, reducing discretionary shopping visits over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if the park surge is accompanied by a matching rise in transit-driven city-center access.
candidate_trigger: PARKS jumps above +10 after a negative week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 11.4 at t-2w before dropping again
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite PARKS moving above +10 without a contemporaneous transit recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT marks easing constraints on movement, which lifts discretionary retail demand with a lag. The effect should be strongest when both series improve together rather than separately.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 10 points and TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points within the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -53.1 to -28.0 by t-0w while TRANSIT stayed weak
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move above its last-28-day mean within four weeks after a same-week rebound in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent outside home, which increases casual shopping and browsing trips. If RESIDENTIAL falls from its current elevated level, RETAIL_REC should improve within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +8 after being above +10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 11.3 at t-1w and was still 8.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL drops below +8 from a higher level.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remains negative while GROCERY_PHARM also weakens, it signals that even local errands and short outings are suppressed, which should pull RETAIL_REC lower over the next month. The signal is a broad-demand weakness rather than a single-category shock.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM were both negative by t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM stay below zero for the next four weeks.
